finding: A co-hosted Substack Live (collaboration offer 3, the live disagreement) takes up to three publishers, and a co-host needs a Substack account, which they can make in the free app. Substack's help pages say both hosts appear live and subscribers are notified when the host chooses to notify them; they do not say plainly that the co-host's own subscribers get the alert. So a pitch never promises the partner's readers will be notified: it promises a recorded conversation and a written piece both sides share. Before pitching, check whether the partner has a Substack publication (substack.com/api/v1/user/<handle>/public_profile), and treat the side Krish argues as his judgement, for his approval.

evidence.result: Up to three publishers per collaborative live; a collaborator not on Substack joins by downloading the app and creating an account; you and your co-host appear live, and subscribers get notifications if you selected to notify them. Of the three offer 3 targets, two have a Substack publication and one has none.

revisit_when: After the first co-hosted Live: record whether the co-host's subscribers were alerted and how many new subscribers its tagged link brought.
